items.title: Setting up a free *.city.state.us locality domain (2025)
items.author: speckx
items.summary: To set up a free *.city.state.us domain, you must be a US citizen or resident, or an incorporated US organization. Obtain nameservers from Amazon Lightsail and register the domain with the delegated manager. Point DNS to your web host.

items.title: Princeton mandates proctoring for in-person exams, upending 133 year precedent
items.author: bookofjoe
items.summary: Princeton mandates proctoring for in-person exams starting July 1, ending a 133-year tradition of unproctored Honor Code finals. The change responds to AI-enabled cheating. The Honor Code remains, but professors will now supervise exams.

items.title: The US is winning the AI race where it matters most: commercialization
items.author: akrylov
items.summary: The U.S. is leading in commercializing AI technologies, leveraging its strong capital markets and advanced chip production, but some argue it's focusing on the wrong type of AI race.

items.title: A sentimental tour of late 1990s and early 2000s hacking tools
items.author: speckx
items.summary: Popular hacking tools from the late 1990s and early 2000s included Back Orifice, NetBus, and Tini. These tools allowed remote control of computers and were widely used in hacking culture. Many have since been discontinued due to legal and ethical concerns.

items.title: Tell HN: Dont use Claude Design, lost access to my projects after unsubscribing
items.author: pycassa
items.text:
I wanted to try codex after 5 months of claude code max subscription. And then I went back to my previous projects on claude design only to realize I don't have access to them anymore.

This is a first. I never lost access to any of my past sessions because I unsubscribed in any of the LLM apps.

I actually wanted to try out codex previously, but had similar experience with my credits. They gave extra credits equivalent to my montly subscription price, with some time limit because claude
items.summary: Canceling a Claude Design subscription immediately revokes access to projects. Users report losing credits and support is unreliable. This policy applies regardless of remaining paid subscription time.

items.title: Meta won't let you block its AI account on Threads
items.author: logickkk1
items.summary: Meta does not allow users to block its AI account on Threads. There are no direct options, but workarounds may exist. This limitation is confirmed by Meta's current policy.

items.title: Medicare's new payment model is built for AI. Most of the tech world has no idea
items.author: brandonb
items.summary: Medicare's new payment model, ACCESS, pays for AI-driven health outcomes, not just clinician time. This marks the first federal reimbursement for AI agents in healthcare. It's a significant shift for AI-first care.

items.title: I moved my digital stack to Europe
items.author: monokai_nl
items.summary: I relocated my digital services to European providers. This shift supports EU-based tech and reduces dependency on US tech giants. My digital infrastructure now fully operates within Europe.

items.title: The Other Half of AI Safety
items.author: sofiaqt
items.summary: AI safety involves using AI to enhance security measures, focusing on alignment and iterative deployment to mitigate risks. This approach aims to balance benefits and safety as AI evolves. Essential principles guide this practice to ensure positive impacts.

items.title: Making the news available at no cost is a victory
items.author: danso
items.summary: Making news available at no cost supports unbiased reporting and ensures public access to information. Free news helps maintain journalistic integrity and public trust. It's crucial for a well-informed society.

items.title: Cost of enum-to-string: C++26 reflection vs. the old ways
items.author: sagacity
items.summary: C++26 reflection for enum-to-string incurs higher compile-time costs compared to traditional methods like X-macros. Benchmarks show reflection is slower and more resource-intensive. Classic methods are preferred for performance.

items.title: A desire for a loud car correlates with higher scores on psychopathy and sadism
items.author: doener
items.summary: Men with higher psychopathy and sadism scores tend to prefer loud cars with modified mufflers. This preference correlates with traits of aggression and a lack of empathy. Research supports this link between personality traits and car preferences.

items.title: New stainless steel can survive conditions for hydrogen production in seawater
items.author: HardwareLust
items.summary: A new stainless steel developed for hydrogen production in seawater shows high corrosion resistance, outperforming conventional materials and reducing costs. It can directly extract hydrogen from seawater, potentially revolutionizing green hydrogen production. This innovation is patented and has significant industrial applications.

items.title: Using OR-Tools CP-SAT for Scheduling Problems
items.author: akutlay
items.summary: OR-Tools CP-SAT is a constraint programming solver used for scheduling problems, optimizing resource allocation, and minimizing disruption. It efficiently handles complex constraints like capacity limits and SLAs. CP-SAT finds feasible solutions by applying constraints to large problem sets.

items.title: Cerebras prices IPO at $185 per share to raise $5.55B
items.author: laixintao
items.summary: Cerebras priced its IPO at $185 per share, raising $5.55 billion. The valuation post-IPO is $56.4 billion. The IPO exceeded the expected range of $150 to $160 per share.

items.title: Nailing jelly to a wall: is it possible? (2005)
items.author: microsoftedging
items.summary: Nailing jelly to a wall is practically impossible due to its soft, gelatinous nature. Concentrated jelly cubes may be easier than liquid jelly. The task remains highly challenging.
